item.title: Re: Tale about the fall of the SCP Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Heya.

To boil this down, it seems to be a researcher experiencing a k-class scenario. We have quite a few tales and canons set in situations like this, as well as SCP-5000. So how are you going to make yours unique, what is going to make me want to read this tale about an apocalypse rather than others?

This previous point ties into your hook. Just having to "survive" isn't inherently interesting, what is his goal or is he just aimless, what logical conclusion do you want the tale to have. Alternatively, is there something about him being a containment engineer that makes the story special? Add something to develop your story and the character further.

Hope this helped.

item.title: Re: The "Uncontainable" SCP
item.content:encoded:
This was worth the wait my man, thanks.

So are you from Sesame Street...
Or more Kermit the frog?

Not everything needs a backstory

I just didn't want to say "It just happened one day." y'know?

lack of connection to Chicago Spirit

Down one of these crit chains I came up with this: They are a poor immigrant with their family, and have to join CS at age 16 to make ends meet. They choose the spirit because Para-Crime pays more than the competitors. They start as a pickpocket, but after the spirit realize they made him anomalous, he get promoted to "Heist Plan-B"

The description here took me a second to understand what was going on.

I was trying to be concise, so here is a description of the blood creature

A humanoid made entirely of SCP-XXX's blood. It stands at a height of 180 centimeter, same as SCP-XXX. The blood appears to be flowing. To date, it has never successfully been terminated other than by completing SCP-XXX's escape.

this feels somewhat farfetched due to the (supposed) criminal background this person has.

In a job interview the foundation conducts, he says he was only committing crime for the money. This would cause them to assume hiring him would cause him to stop. The first crime while employed is botched and almost caused the anomalous properties to manifest, but the foundation steps in and tells them, "Sigh, ok, we called in a few police favors for you there. Why? Because we thought we saw something in you. Prove to us we shouldn't have let you rot in a cell." This gets him to stop.

I'll add a timeline of events for you and other critters on the main post.

<3 thanks again <3

item.title: The Electrical Girl
item.content:encoded:
Special Containment Procedures:

SCP-5127 is kept in site 19 and to be kept in a 15 by15 meter room guarded by two guards out side of the container to avoid containment breach.

There are to be two back up generators within 100 meters of SCP-5127’s containment. No SCP’s are allowed within 150 meters of SCP-5127 including any unauthorized personnel (Class D is allowed for testing).

All guards guarding SCP-5127 are to be striped of any electrical equipment and are to put the equipment in a steel box out side of the 100 meter parameters.

SCP-5127 is to have entertainment at all times to avoid boredom which unconsciously causes a electromagnetic pulse which can cause a containment breach.

Description:
SCP-5127 is what appears to be a fourteen year old girl who has the ability to cause lethal electromagnetic pulses uncontrollably this is prevented by SCP-5127 having entertainment to prevent boredom. SCP-5127 also has a defense mechanism in which (if pierced by metal) causes an electrical shock killing the holder of the metal (see incident 5127-1) SCP-5127 immediately feels guilt after death of personnel except Class D personnel. Researchers assigned to SCP-5127 noted SCP-5127 is aware of Class D’s actions and knows there in the foundation as testing for a reason

item.title: Re: No Happy Endings
item.content:encoded:
We then get an exploration log of the kingdom, as they arrive in the ruins of a large theatre. They move through the kingdom, which, while beautiful, is heavily damaged from a series of fires.

So I am pretty confused here, what kingdom is this? is it some fictional universe or alternate dimension the foundation are traveling to? If there's no explanation how a magical fairytale kingdom exists in the same world as the foundation without somehow being obfuscated from the public, I will lose my immersion pretty much immediately.

I still suggest not using a fake country, unless it is some magical land explained in the article, for the same reason. The reason SCPs work (in my opinion) is that they're set in a realistic rendition of our world with the strange being hidden away… but a whole magical kingdom is gonna stretch my disbelief.

Now… This does not necessarily have to be the case in a tale, but even then, I feel like there's still some need to explain how this magical land has not been in our history forever.

I think this needs to be more grounded, personally.

item.title: Re: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France
item.content:encoded:
/scp-5144 (A Multiversal Joyride) by Wolfmandeth deleted at -20 and three votes.

Item #: SCP-5144

AKA: A Multiversal Joyride

Object Class: Safe | Euclid | Keter

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-5144 is 3 4 5 separate entities/objects. 5144-2 and 5144-3 have been contained but 5144-1 cannot be contained by any means in this reality (See SCP-5144-1 log for details).

Feedback ported:

[+] from Quicksilvers
– hide block

I can see that you've put a lot of effort into this article since its a real long one, but there is a lot that can be rewritten or reworked.

SCP nicknames are never actually referenced in the main document. It usually only there on the mainlist or when in casual conversation - no actual SCP document refers to the anomalies by their nicknames. The syntax is off throughout the article and isn't clinical enough to read as an actual SCP document too. You use a lot of images here but a lot of them don't seem to be licensed under creative commons. That means that you using them in this article infringes upon the original creators' copyright.

The dialogue is a little too stiff for segments like the breaches and interviews. By "stiff," I mean that it doesn't sound that realistic? The scientists either seem too robotic or too casual depending on the scenario, and they don't really speak like analytical scientists.

Another thing about your piece is that the format of the actual document is very jarring and doesn't fit the normal style of an SCP report. You explain the anomaly too much in the Special Containment Procedures when it should actually be described in a "Description" subsection that is missing entirely. The lack of a main Description segment also doesn't help since some readers immediately jump to the Description segment of an SCP document without reading the Containment Protocols - no main description could be a deterrent to people who open the article and glance to see there isn't something concise.

Now, the sub-anomalies are a little all over the place. Each sub-anomaly has so much to it that they each could possibly be categorized as their own SCP within themselves instead of cramming them all into a single document. I'd advise that if you're planning to revise and keep going with this concept, you split the whole document up into multiple different SCP a la DJKaktus's fey war mythos. I can see you're probably aiming for an interesting interwoven story like 4812, but everything sort of collides into each other instead of meshing together. You also have a slight tendency to have these really strange descriptions - with -1, its over-described, yet with -2, -3, and -4, they're under-described. There's also things sprinkled in throughout the document that don't fit the bill - the "cry for help" broadcast in another language, the unnecessary crosstests with popular SCPs, and whatever… this is…

SCP-5144-1 has no sexual attraction to humans. However, it has shown interest in SCP-1472, claiming that Dr. Bright said something about Velociraptors in maid costumes. SCP-5144-1 has sent 4 requests to Dr. Paul Blart for permission to enter SCP-1472, permission has been denied.

I don't know, it just doesn't sit well with the reader.

That's all I really have to say - needs a LOT of reworking but it can eventually be fleshed out into a good article.

Best of luck!

[+] from Mikaelious
– hide block

This is probably longer than any article on the site. While length isn't necessarily a bad thing, you're gonna have to make it more than captivating if you don't want the readers to lose interest.

item.title: The day the foundation needed help with Gamer Against Weed
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Page Layout: The page will begin with a simple description of the SCP and after that, the investigation of containing it.

Elevator Pitch: We can see the researcher ask for a member of Gamer Against Weed to help him to contain SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: Ok, so basically, the SCP is a drug that makes all the people that sniff it is all good and all of that. The anomaly is that it can't be stopped and will have some kind of dependence over it even when all the traces of it are being wiped out. So there's a containment breach over the site that contains it and the foundation try all they can to contain SCP-XXXX. A scientist has this idea about cooperating with Gamer Against Weed because of their experience with the drug SCP. Of course, the chance of GAW having actually experience with the drugs SCP is really little but it's their only chance. So the researcher that has found the idea will communicate with GAW and try to cooperate with them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The originality of my idea is that we never actually get to have Gamer Against Weed to be more serious and actually be not the kind of Goi that is just here for the laughs. Of course, they will still be the classic version.

item.title: Re: A strange foundation(seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Although this does seem intriguing I don't really like most of the ideas presented here. Also, for the page layout, you can just say there will be multiple iterations of the article that are still gonna be readable. This Foundation being made up entirely of anomalies themselves that only contain what we perceive as regular animals (maybe if you explored the reason they contain them and revealed that the wildlife are actually anomalies or something we aren't aware of) is something I could bite on. The rest I don't like.

You say they have one(1) site but then immediately tell us about three(3) different ones. Not to mention you stated that their language was impossible to decode but then say that they establish communication and talk with our Foundation? What do you mean by multiple terminations? Like did the Foundation just casually wipe out this Foundation multiple times or their entire species and they just keep popping back up? I have no idea why our Foundation would merge with this Foundation, at the most I think our Foundation would just establish an alliance-ish thing with them. They're pretty much useless to the Foundation and unless they pose an actual threat or can help the Foundation at all besides just abducting cows then I don't really see how that would happen.

this Foundation also has almost nothing in common with our Foundation besides containing wildlife instead of anomalies so I don't really know that attention grabber makes sense
